about: What a GENERATED Swift artifact answers differently from ECMA-262 for a
reason that is not about the language at all: a case the code generator
mishandles (a guard evaluated twice, an expression written to the wrong
place), as opposed to one the frontend lowers wrongly.
The two are kept apart on purpose. `ecma262_emitted_lua.json` and the
engine's own table test hold what the FRONTEND lowers, and an entry here
would say something else: that the Lua is right and the machine around it
is not. Folding one into the other sends the next reader to the wrong
half of the seam.
HELD IN BOTH DIRECTIONS by `Ecma262LoweredArtifactTests`. An entry whose
case the artifact now answers CORRECTLY is red: remove it, because a list
that can only grow can never reach zero, and zero is the point. An
undeclared wrong answer is red too. Neither direction has an escape
hatch: a case is either right, or named here with a cause someone can act
on.
AND A CEILING. `maxDefects` in that suite refuses a list that has grown
past a handful, and `ecma262-lowered-swift` keeps a SECOND ceiling over the
`codegen-defects=` count the suite prints, in another language, so raising
the constant in the file that reads it is not enough. An exclusion list
with no ceiling is a way to make any lane green; this one is small on
purpose, and every entry is a defect someone is expected to remove.
The list is empty, which is the intended steady state and not a sign the
file is unused: it is the contract that keeps it empty.
Each entry names `source` and `clause` exactly as `ecma262_semantics.json`
spells them (`source` alone does not identify a case: the table asks `a && b`
under two clauses), and carries a `cause` that says what the generator does.
